launches.tagline: Let AI shop for you without exposing your card.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Allowance lets AI agents safely make purchases on behalf of users using one-time virtual cards with built-in guardrails.

<https://youtu.be/i-V5uPtKEew>

## The Problem

AI agents can now browse websites, research products and complete real-world tasks autonomously, but they cannot complete purchases for you.

Using AI to buy something usually has meant pasting your real credit card into a prompt and giving an agent unrestricted spending access. That’s dangerous.

## The Solution

Allowance solves this by giving AI agents one-time virtual cards with approval controls and built-in limits. The AI agent never sees the user’s real card number.

Users can:\
• limit spending amounts\
• restrict purchases to specific merchants\
• approve or deny purchases in real time\
• revoke access anytime\
• continue using their existing credit cards and rewards

This unlocks entirely new use cases for AI-powered commerce:\
• planning and booking travel, hotels, and flights autonomously within user-defined limits\
• tracking products that are out of stock and instantly purchasing them when inventory returns\
• securely placing food orders, reservations, ticket purchases, and ecommerce checkouts on a user’s behalf\
• monitoring prices and automatically buying when something drops below a target price\
• using AI not just to research products, but to actually complete the purchase end-to-end\
• letting agents handle repetitive purchases and checkouts across the web

The recent progress in AI agents, new payment protocols, and browser automation makes it increasingly clear that agents will eventually transact across the internet on behalf of users. Safe guardrails and user-controlled payments infrastructure are the missing layer that makes this possible.

I’ve been using Allowance to place real-world purchases through AI agents including food orders, reservations, and ecommerce checkouts using one-time virtual cards with approval controls.

## The Ask

Try the product, tell me what you’re using it for, how it could better fit into your life, and share feedback. Start here: [useallowance.com](https://useallowance.com/)

I’d especially love to hear new ideas for agentic purchasing use cases and guardrails.

## About Me

I’m Dasmer, founder of Allowance.

I started building Allowance after running into this problem myself while trying to book a reservation using OpenClaw. The agent successfully navigated the flow, but then asked me to paste in my credit card number to hold the reservation. That felt fundamentally wrong — and made it obvious the missing layer for agentic commerce was safe, user-controlled payments.\
Before Allowance, I was Head of Product for Cash App Families, where I helped grow Cash App into the most popular debit card for teens in the US. Earlier in my career, I was also an early iOS engineer at Venmo.

Before River Markets, **Oscar** built models trading multi-billion dollar portfolios at BlackRock. **Antonin** built high-frequency trading strategies at Valkyrie.

launches.body:
**_TL;DR:_** Soria is an AI-native Financial Terminal for investors who specialize in a particular sector, starting with healthcare. Our agents convert hundreds of the most important public and private sources into an always-on financial model, reviewed by domain experts and delivered to hedge funds, banks, and asset managers through a terminal UI, MCP, API, warehouse sync, and research feed. Unlike our competitors, we own the data layer and expand bottom-up, one sector at a time - additionally our agents proactively do research on behalf of our clients without them lifting a finger or sharing any data.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tgfT9DDbNQ>

Today [**Cameron Spiller**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cameron-spiller-b316b850/) and I are excited to launch **Soria**, an AI research terminal built specifically for healthcare investors in public markets.

I spent 8 years as a VP in Equity Research at Bank of America covering healthcare and serving hundreds of hedge fund, private equity, and VC clients. Soria is the platform I always wished I had. Cameron is a serial founding engineer and CTO who has spent the last decade building fintech startups, always from <5 people all the way to billion dollar plus outcomes.

In addition to YC we are backed by the founders of GLG, as well as other industry insiders, and we recently won BattleFin’s #1 New Data Vendor award. **We already serve teams at many of the largest banks, hedge funds, and asset managers in the world, managing >$1T in assets**. Our users are fundamental equity analysts, often people who have spent years or decades covering healthcare.

The core problem is simple: the research process is still too manual, time-intensive, error-prone, and fragmented. Analysts waste up to 1/3 of their time doing repetitive work that doesn’t even generate alpha. Meanwhile, most solutions including Bloomberg are too generalized, they offer almost nothing relevant to healthcare or other domain specific verticals.

Soria ingests the most important public and private sources healthcare analysts actually care about, structures them into an always-updated sector model. Pre-AI the domain context just didn’t scale.

We are differentiated in three critical ways:

**1. Soria is proactive. It’s like an OpenClaw agent that you don’t have to set up.**

There is **zero setup**. From day one, analysts receive updates on the most important data points, curated and reviewed by actual research analysts. Every day we add more sources, and the model gets better without users needing to configure or maintain anything.

**2. Soria requires no data sharing.**

We do not need to integrate into a bank or fund to be useful. We build the research and data layer ourselves, then deliver the **output** however the customer wants it: terminal UI, MCP, API, warehouse sync, or email.

**3. Soria builds coverage one sector at a time.**

Most AI finance tools help analysts work faster, but still leave the job of sector coverage to the analyst. Soria can do that work upfront because we are hyper-specialized.

For healthcare services teams, Soria can consolidate $200k+ of annual vendor spend across products like Milliman, HMA, Mark Farrah, AHD, Daloopa, FactSet, and NAIC, while also absorbing a large portion of the repetitive associate-level data work that doesn’t scale.

That’s just the first sector, there are 228 globally. Our vision: as we build out each sector, we consolidate it into a model of healthcare, the US and eventually the world.

name: Klaimee
long_description:
Klaimee is the first insurance for your AI agents. It covers what traditional E&O and cyber explicitly carve out, so you can deploy agentic AI at scale with real peace of mind.
Built for companies deploying agentic AI, self-serve from day one.

The problem: AI agents are taking actions autonomously buying, emailing, modifying sensitive data. AB 316 already holds deployers liable. EU AI Act enforces in August. Cyber and E&O insurance are excluding AI claims. Companies shipping agents have zero coverage and no third-party proof their agent is safe. Enterprise legal asks "who pays if your agent breaks something?" and there's no good answer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
We built the answer. Critical-category risk evaluation, certification, financial guarantee, liability insurance and the documentation enterprise procurement needs to sign off.

Team: Ines (ex-General Manager at SafetyWing, grew insurance product from $5M to $60M revenue, 5 years launching insurance products from scratch and structuring a TokioMarine MGA into its own carrier) + Julien (AI software engineer + corporate strategy, enterprise compliance).

We understand how insurance works, what enterprises require, and why startups can't wait 6 months for either.
one_liner: Liability insurance for AI Agents. You deploy agents, we cover you.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
AI agents can now execute financial transactions, access sensitive data, and take real-world actions, but there is no insurance, no certification, and no clear liability framework for when they fail.

This is the same gap that existed with cyber risk in the early 2000s, before a $15B+ insurance market emerged. We’re at that same inflection point with AI.

The signals are already there: AI-related incidents are being carved out of traditional liability coverage, lawsuits are growing rapidly, and enterprises are still under pressure to deploy AI. The result is a fast-growing, unaddressed risk layer.

We saw this firsthand. We were building AI agents for claims processing: handling payments and decisions inside regulated environments. Every customer asked the same question: who is liable when the agent gets it wrong? There was no answer.

That’s when it became clear: this infrastructure has to exist before enterprise AI can scale.

Ines had already built insurance products from zero at SafetyWing, including carrier relationships and underwriting frameworks. We realized we were uniquely positioned to build the certification and insurance layer for AI agents - so we did.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every transformative technology needs a trust layer before it can scale.\
The internet needed cybersecurity. Cloud computing needed compliance and audit standards.

AI is next.

Today, AI agents can act but they can’t be trusted at scale. There is no standard for how they’re evaluated, no clear liability when they fail, and no infrastructure to make them safe to deploy in critical environments.

If we succeed, the liability and certification framework we build won't just protect enterprises, it will make AI itself safer, more accountable, and more auditable at a global scale. We are not just selling insurance. We are building the infrastructure that allows the agentic world to exist.

launches.title: Klaimee insures your AI Agents
launches.tagline: Klaimee is the first purpose-build E&O coverage for AI agents.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: [Klaimee](https://klaimee.ai) is the first insurance for your AI agents. It covers what traditional E&O and cyber explicitly carve out, so you can deploy agentic AI at scale with real peace of mind.**

80% of Fortune 500 companies are already using AI agents. That’s creating a new kind of liability risk no one is really covering yet.\
Enterprises want AI. But they want to know “who pays if something goes wrong”? There’s no clear answer today.\
Meanwhile, AI-related lawsuits are up 137% between 2024 and 2025.

> 👋 Hi, we are Ines and Julien.\
> [Ines](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ines-boutemadja/) was General Manager at SafetyWing (W18), she spent the last 5 years building insurance products from scratch, structured a Tokio Marine MGA, and got the Puerto Rico carrier license, scaling an insurance startup from $5M to $60M. She ran this playbook before, doing it again, AI-native this time.\
> [Julien](https://www.linkedin.com/in/julien-catonnet/) handles the engineering and enterprise compliance side. He has a strategy consulting background, working with corporates and insurance, coupled with a deep software engineering and AI expertise.\
> 🔥 Our team brings the best of both worlds to underwrite the new emerging AI risk.

### **💡 The opportunity:**

Traditional insurance was built for deterministic software; it either works or throws an explicit error. AI agents fail silently and not uniformly. So cyber won't cover it. E&O won't cover it either.

The existing insurance industry lacks the velocity and deep AI knowledge to fill this gap.

We built [Klaimee](https://klaimee.ai) to do exactly that: we provide liability insurance, financial guarantee, critical risk evaluation, certification, and procurement documentation enterprises require, all in under 24 hours.

Watch our launch video below <https://youtu.be/Y7VBNr81b5Y>

### **⚙️ How we do it:**

To insure AI agents, we had to reinvent how traditional underwriting works. Our proprietary, three-block system determines an agent’s risk score and insurance price:

1. **Public Data Scan:** We scan publicly available data related to the agent.
2. **Governance Assessment:** We ask 30 questions concerning the agent’s governance.
3. **Behavioral Testing:** We actually test your agent’s behavior, firing more than 100 probes (prompt injection, jailbreak, decision drift, data leakage, biased outputs) to understand _when_ and _how_ it fails.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100700&key=user_uploads/2955371/49d6f4de-8787-48c4-a6b2-728323148e81)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100700&key=user_uploads/2955371/9ebe5a9c-7ce0-4d29-b3f5-c7017ca8d0d7)

**Score it. Certify it. Underwrite it. Insure it ▷ with a 24h turnaround.**

We bring the trust layers so startups and enterprises can deploy agentic AI with peace of mind.

### **🛡️ What we cover: AI agents in healthcare and biotech, finance & accounting, IT & software development, law & legal tech, customers support and sales agents.**

AI Agents act like humans: they take actions, make decisions, and have a real impact that can cause damages. At[ Klaimee](https://klaimee.ai), we cover the actual behavior of the AI agents. Real failure modes happening in production right now:

* An agent hallucinated a contract clause your customer relied on.
* An agent leaked one patient’'s data to another.
* An agent made a biased call in lending, hiring, or pricing.
* An agent took an unauthorized action with financial damage downstream.

### **⌛️ Why now:**

Major insurers like Berkshire, Chubb, and Travelers are winning state approval to exclude AI liability from standard commercial policies, leaving every agent-deploying company exposed. And it is leaving every agent-deploying company exposed.

The ISO, which sets standards for 70% of the U.S. market, is making AI exclusions the default for Commercial General Liability policies (ISO CG 40 47 / CG 40 48 endorsements). The EU AI Act enforces in August 2026.

Every Fortune 500 procurement team is now asking the AI insurance question, and the answer from incumbents is "we exclude that."

The same thing happened with cyber 20 years ago. It got carved out of existing policies. A whole new line of insurance was created. The same shift is happening with AI right now. And nobody has built the product for it yet.

Ines has done this in insurance before. Julien goes deep on the AI side. Together we know how to actually price the risk.

We understand what enterprise buyers need to see, and why a startup can’t sit around for 6 months waiting on a traditional carrier.

If you’re shipping AI agents into enterprise, you should already be thinking about coverage.

### We’re underwriting our first cohort now → [**klaimee.ai**](http://klaimee.ai)

launches.body:
A letter arrives in the mail.

Impossible to understand.

Another one.

Then the phone calls start.

Once a day. Unpleasant, sometimes hostile.

This is how debt collection works in 2026.

**We’re here to fix it.**\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X9mVp2ZyJMUhCcHN6NadzMNLV5S63Wpv](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X9mVp2ZyJMUhCcHN6NadzMNLV5S63Wpv/view?usp=sharing)

# TL;DR

Audun is an AI-native debt collection company. Our agents automate the collections process end to end, from reminders and negotiations to back-office and legal work. This reduces collection costs for creditors, and enables humans to spend their time on the conversations that matter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111293&key=user_uploads/3587634/839f47e4-cdd7-45ed-befd-c621930fef65)

# Ask

We’re looking for introductions to collection leaders at banks, lenders, utilities, telcos, and other high-volume creditors.

# The problem

The debt collection industry is broken. It runs on call centers, paper letters, and software built in the 90s. While the rest of the world is preparing for AGI, the topic of the industry is still email and cloud.

All these inefficiencies ultimately end up with the consumer: incomprehensible letters arriving by snail mail, hostile phone calls, and fees stacking up on a bill they may never have seen. They're paying the cost of an archaic system.

# The solution

Audun is an AI-native debt collection company. We automate up to 90% of cases across the whole business, from front to back office. Our agents manage reminders, negotiations, payment plans, and settlements across voice, SMS, email, and WhatsApp. They operate within creditor-defined rules, log every action, and escalate sensitive cases to humans with the full context attached. Behind the scenes, they handle tasks such as skip tracing, payment verification, and legal document drafting.

By automating the grunt work of collections, Audun lowers collection costs for creditors and, ultimately, borrowing costs for consumers. We enable people to focus on the conversations that matter, where human judgment is still required, giving customers the treatment they deserve.

We started out in the Nordics, which has some of the strictest collections regulation in the world. Compliance is critical in this industry, so we built our agents to handle the toughest version of it first. 

# Who we are

We’re four founders with experience across McKinsey, Midjourney, and Norway’s first unicorn. We’ve seen firsthand how manual this industry is, and how stuck the incumbents are. We decided to build the company this industry needs from the ground up.

launches.tagline: GPU marketplace where vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. $300M+ in RFQs in our first month.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** AI hardware trades over phone calls and forwarded spreadsheets. No venue, no price to mark against: lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals. We're building Stoa, an RFQ marketplace where buyers and sellers get firm quotes within 48 hours, and settled trades build the prices the market can mark, finance, and hedge against.

<https://youtu.be/zbD21BgAo88>

GPU deals close in group chats. We know because we've been in them.

A price arrives as a voice note. Someone forwards an inventory list, then it gets forwarded again, and soon three brokers are offering the same machines. Nobody knows who actually owns what or whether any quote is firm.

The market behind those chats is worth hundreds of billions of dollars a year. Lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals, not trades.

We're Berat, Eren, and Kaan. We're building Stoa.

AI hardware is becoming an asset class, but its market is missing the basics: a venue where hardware can trade, prices that buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against, and eventually financing and hedging built on those prices. We're starting with the venue: an RFQ marketplace for GPUs. It gets buyers and sellers firm quotes, and every bid and settlement builds the history the rest needs.

**Here's how it works**

Post what you want to buy or sell: B300s, H200s, H100s, a bare card or a full cluster, new or secondary.

Vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. Instead of spending weeks calling around, you get through the RFQ in 48 hours.

We handle the unglamorous parts too: KYB and counterparty checks, contracts, shipping, and settlement.

In our first month, $300M+ in RFQs ran through the book.

**Why the marketplace comes first**

Ask what an H100 is worth and everyone you call gives you a different answer.

On Stoa, dealers quote against the same RFQ without seeing each other's bids. Because every RFQ, firm quote, award, and settlement runs through us, we see what the hardware actually trades for.

A quote is an opinion. A settled trade is a receipt.

That transaction history becomes prices buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against. Once marks are grounded in settled trades, financing and hedging can follow.

Platts started printing oil prices in a magazine. Kelley Blue Book began as one dealer's published list of what he'd pay for cars. GPU inventory is still being passed around in forwarded spreadsheets, and Blackwell upgrades are now pushing H100 fleets into the secondary market.

Someone is going to be the price.

**The team**

We've known each other for more than ten years. We have founded companies, traded interest rate derivatives, and built trading and pricing infrastructure for oil and gas. Now we're building it for AI hardware.

**Buying or selling?**

If you're buying GPUs or compute, or you're sitting on hardware, sign up at [stoaexchange.com](http://stoaexchange.com).

**Schedule a call: [https://stoa.cal.com/stoa/intro](https://stoa.cal.com/stoa/intro)**

**Email us: [founders@stoaexchange.com](mailto:founders@stoaexchange.com)**

**Text or call us:** +1 510 605 3844

And if you know infrastructure heads at neoclouds or data centers, hyperscaler capex teams, dealers, ITADs, or credit desks lending against GPUs, please send this their way.

Berat, Eren & Kaan

launches.body:
TL;DR: Spectre Capital is a multi-strategy trading firm run by AI agents, not human analysts. We deploy real capital to capture every decision, reasoning trace, and ground-truth outcome, so our agents learn and compound from every mistake. Most AI trading labs pay egregious amounts for training data. Ours pays us when we win.

We left Harvard after starting a hedge fund from our college dorm (go Currier!).

Now we’re building Spectre Intelligence, a neotrading firm training superhuman AI traders. 

**The problem**

Intelligence is getting cheaper, and it will rewire trading. But the scarcest input to markets isn't compute or data feeds or latency, but rather judgment. That data is fragmented, scarce, and the foundation of entire careers. It is also entirely proprietary and guarded fiercely by firms.

**What we do**

We collect judgment by trading live. Every position our agents take generates decisions, full reasoning traces, and ground-truth P&L. We think this is the ultimate alignment of incentives in one of the largest TAMs in the world.

The structure is evolutionary from first principles: open competition inside each pod, and strategies and pods are born and killed constantly. 

Unlike a traditional pod shop, spinning up a new pod costs compute, not headcount. Our agents work superhuman hours, monitor a superhuman number of things, and learn from every real and simulated trade. Our AI traders develop specialized strategies in parallel, allowing us to scale far beyond the limits of human bandwidth. This is an edge that scales, compounds, and isn't held by any one employee.

**Traction**

\- Two live pods: semiconductors and biotech equities. (We picked the verticals, not our AI traders.)

**Why now?**

AI is the worst it will ever be, LLM traders aren't even good yet, but we believe the writing is on the wall and want to be on the frontier. Quant funds were arguably the first agent labs: ML theory embedded for decades, quants as very expensive agents. We're building the generation after.

**The ask**

If any of this resonates, feel free to reach out: michelle@spectreintelligence.ai

We’re also collecting an expert network across semis + biotech, so if you have experience, feel free to join at <https://www.spectreintelligence.ai/experts>

launches.body:
**TL;DR: Veltha reads an entire claim file, flags what's missing, and applies the exact federal regulation that governs it, producing a citation-backed determination a human adjuster just signs off on. Work that took an adjuster \~6 hours now takes \~10 minutes.** Starting with workers' comp and crop insurance.

<https://www.loom.com/share/9e9701f61bf4400890b4799fdda3d3ff>

**The problem**

1 in 4 claims adjusters expect to retire within five years. Experienced adjusters are retiring faster than carriers can replace them, and processing capacity is now the binding constraint on growth.

**What we built**

Veltha is an AI claims adjuster that runs the whole file end to end:

* **Triage** - reads incoming claim emails and documents, classifies them, and routes each claim to the right workflow.
* **Gap detection** - checks the file for missing documents and records, then requests them by email, phone, or fax and runs follow-up cadences until they land.
* **Compliance review** - applies the relevant federal rulebook, and produces a determination where **every output element is tied to a source span and a specific regulatory provision.**

The adjuster's job shifts from _doing_ the claim to _reviewing_ Veltha's output. Less chasing. Faster decisions. Output that survives an audit.

**What we understand that others don't: regulation is the moat, not the obstacle.** Horizontal platforms (Guidewire, Duck Creek) and generic AI-claims startups can summarize a claim file. They can't tell you _which_ provision triggered _which_ adjustment, with citations. We treat the federal rulebook as an anchor for the workflow we embed within the organisation. That's the difference between a summary a human re-does from scratch and an output an adjuster will actually sign.

**Our ask**

We'd love intros to:

* **Anyone in claims at a carrier, MGA, or TPA** - especially **workers' comp**
* **People at large self-insured employers** with claims-heavy, high-risk workforces - Companies exactly like these are who we're built for: **Disney, Marriott, Ford, PG&E, Caterpillar**. If you know someone at that kind of company, an intro is gold.

launches.tagline: The underwriting system of record for the AI era
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Qlo uses AI agents to run commercial underwriting operations from submission to renewal. We rebuilt the underlying system so agents can operate across the entire workflow, not sit beside another legacy system. One enterprise client signed a two-year contract, went live in May, and has since tripled weekly primary quote throughput. The end state is autonomous underwriting that follows each company’s underwriting judgment and stays within the carrier’s appetite.

Today, we’re launching the **Qlo Inbox Agent**.

<https://youtu.be/aICb20uhqhU>

### The Problem

More than $110B in commercial insurance premium flows through U.S. MGAs every year. Much of the work still begins with an email from a broker.

Commercial underwriters can spend up to 80% of their day in the inbox, chasing missing applications, loss runs, and other submission documents. Even a submission with roughly $50K in annual premium can take 48 hours to turn into a quote.

Once the information arrives, teams still need to prepare the data, run the rater, and assemble the right endorsements and quote variants.

When volume grows, teams add headcount. But underwriting judgment is hard to train and keep consistent. Costs rise, good submissions remain untouched, and inconsistent decisions can hurt loss ratios.

More premium left on the table, now with more people on payroll.

### What We Built

Qlo runs the commercial underwriting workflow from submission to renewal. Specialized agents handle each operational step, while supervisor agents coordinate the work and communicate with the underwriter.

The Inbox Agent is one of those supervisors. An underwriter can message it from a phone like a teammate. It understands the instruction, calls the right subagents, and completes the work inside Qlo.

**The underwriter makes the call. The agents make it happen.**

One of those subagents is the Rater Converter we launched on Bookface. It turns an existing rating spreadsheet into a validated digital worksheet the rest of the workflow can use.

This is what agent-compatible means to us: agents understand the workflow, have the right context, and can act across the system. Today, they execute the underwriter’s decisions. The end state is autonomous underwriting within each company’s judgment, appetite, and controls.

**The party has begun. Let the agents dance on top of Qlo.**

Guidewire and Vertafore helped define the last era of commercial insurance software. We’re building Qlo to define the next one.

### Why Us

Before Qlo, Ryan spent 2.5 years building a commercial insurance marketplace and saw carrier-side systems up close. The company received acquisition terms from a public insurance company, and two founders who were customers there are now advisors to Qlo.

Liv previously led backend at a Taiwanese baby-monitor company generating roughly $15M in annual revenue. Ryan and Liv had already built together before starting Qlo.

We build alongside experienced underwriters who want to help define how commercial insurance will operate in the AI era.

### Our Ask

We’re looking for:

* **Introductions to commercial MGAs and program administrators**, especially submission-heavy programs with complex rating files or underwriting teams hitting the limits of their current systems.
* **Introductions to investors who understand commercial insurance** and see the same path toward autonomous underwriting.
* **Insurance operators with strong opinions about the future of underwriting**. Even if you’re not looking for a new system, we’d still like to learn how your business works.

If you run an MGA or program, want to build with us, or see the same future as an investor, email us at [founders@getqlo.com](mailto:founders@getqlo.com).

Commercial insurance moves slowly because **distribution beats architecture**.

But distribution eventually stops scaling when the architecture underneath it no longer works.

The system that solves the real problem will be adopted. Time will tell.

We’ll keep building.

launches.title: Risklytics: Insurance for the Frontier

launches.body:
**TLDR:** Risklytics is a commercial insurance brokerage for companies building with AI in the physical space, from robot fleets on customer sites to agents running in production. This year many insurance companies stopped covering risks that involve AI. We find the insurers that will still cover it, translate what you're building into terms they can price, and read every clause before anything is signed.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jHTzpKbmZa4>

**The problem**

Starting this year, many insurance companies began excluding coverage for injury and property damage arising out of AI.

For a hardtech company that language reaches everything you do. If AI touched the work anywhere, including the tools your engineers designed it with or the product itself, the insurer can deny the claim.

The problem with these exclusions is that they get added account by account, so the same hardware can be covered at one insurer and excluded at the next, and nothing in the process makes that obvious. It shows up as a form number on the endorsement list attached to your renewal, which is why most founders don't learn they have one until they file a claim.

**Why now**

Physical AI is scaling faster than the insurance market underneath it. Insurance moves slower, and its first instinct with an unfamiliar risk is to exclude it and wait for loss data. Cyber went the same way: exclusions first, then specialists who understood it, then a real market. AI is at the exclusion stage now, and these companies pushing the frontier can't wait for the cycle to finish on its own. 

**What we do**

We handle the whole coverage process end to end.

You send us an application. We take what you're building and put it in terms an insurance company can understand and price.

Then we go to market. We have access to hundreds of insurance companies, the ones that actually write this kind of risk, and we take your file to them. Most will pass. The few that want it compete on price and terms, and we keep shopping until every requirement you have is met, including the limits your customer contracts demand.

When offers come back we read the policies line by line. If an AI exclusion is attached, we push to get it removed, or we find a company that writes the AI coverage in on purpose. Then we tell you in plain terms what you've got.

We cover the lines your company actually needs: general liability, umbrella, property, equipment in transit and on customer sites, workers' comp, professional liability, management liability, and cyber.

You never pay us. The insurance company pays us a commission out of the premium when a policy is placed, so applying costs you nothing and there's no additional fee from us at any point.

**Where this goes**

Physical AI is expanding faster than any industry, and every company in it buys insurance every year for as long as it exists. The programs grow as the fleets grow.

We want to be the brokerage that grows with them: the people who know this risk best, hold the relationships with the markets that write it, and build the loss data of the future.

**Why us**

We're Sam and Alex, on leave from Harvard. We were already in insurance building models when we noticed that batch mates building some of the most innovative technology in the world couldn't get covered at all. Since then we’ve landed partnerships to offer these frontier companies easier access to better policies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110197&key=user_uploads/2666435/74c5c462-a2ff-44b8-ac6c-f8ebc7807dbd)


**The ask**

If you're building anything on the frontier, apply at[ risklytics.ai](http://risklytics.ai). It takes a few minutes, it costs nothing, and we'll come back with what the market says.

It doesn't matter what you have in place today. If you're building, we want to get you covered.

And if you're an insurer, MGA or wholesaler with appetite here, we want to talk:[ risklytics.ai/markets](https://www.risklytics.ai/markets/)

It's the same story across all of an analyst’s workflows (like new deals, monitoring, reporting, workouts). One example: to borrow against a credit facility (it’s like a credit card for fintechs with a limit typically in the $100Ms ), a team produces and verifies compliance certificates by hand. That's hours of Excel every time, so they draw less often than they should, leaving millions on the table.

**What is Levocred?**

Levocred is an AI employee for your credit team. It plugs into your loan tapes, credit agreements, servicer reports, and bank feeds, learns how you work, and runs the workflows your analysts do by hand today.

* Analyzes new deals and drafts the investment memos
* Monitors the portfolio, marks valuations, and answers questions in Slack ("what's our exposure to X?")
* Produces and checks compliance certificates, and handles covenant and LP reporting

Why it works when nothing else has:

* **It's AI-native, not a rules engine.** Older tools only work if you hand-code every rule, so they break on messy, real-world data. Levocred's agents read your actual documents and tapes and reason across them. We already run consumer, fintech, litigation finance, and MCA through the same engine.
* **You stay in control** with full auditability and no waiting on a vendor's engineers
* **It compounds.** Every document you load makes it smarter about your book. That data moat is yours. It’s why usage only grows.

The result: a draw that took a day of Excel takes minutes, monitoring runs continuously instead of monthly, and your team spends its time on judgment, not grunt work.

* **Mohit Gupta (CEO)**: Studied CS at IIT Bombay (ranked 53rd of 1.2M in the JEE) and Finance at UC Berkeley. Founding engineer at a credit hedge fund, where he later managed a $200M book.
* **Saksham (CTO)**: Previously Software Engineer at a credit fund, where he built and scaled infrastructure as the fund grew. Electrical & Electronics from IIT Kanpur

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Pennant is building AI-native proxy voting solutions for institutional investors, public companies, and their advisors. We’re live with paying enterprise customers, including one of the largest US public pension plans, a Top AmLaw 100 firm, and leading governance advisors. Before Pennant, our team built trillion-dollar tech at BlackRock, cast proxy votes at State Street, and advised Fortune 100 boards at PJT.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_WDs1VB213EcPS5caE5XK7L6UkZLz07l](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_WDs1VB213EcPS5caE5XK7L6UkZLz07l/preview)

**The problem:** Proxy voting at publicly traded companies drives trillions in market value every year. Shareholder votes decide $100B mergers, trillion-dollar pay packages, and the boardroom battles that define companies.

Yet the work is brutally manual: reviewing thousands of pages of SEC filings, research, and engagement notes that live in a patchwork of PDFs, spreadsheets, and post-it notes. And for professional advice, the market has relied on two firms, ISS and Glass Lewis, for 40+ years, a duopoly that controls 97% of the market.

**Why Now:** Technological change and market sentiment are ripping this market wide open.

CEOs have been sounding the proxy-advisor alarm for years:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/45604eff-9d48-4271-90ed-b3bf6000b461)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/a5232d8f-91b7-44bd-8116-f0d251b764d0)

And now big investors and the White House are taking action.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/12da7f65-6e5c-4e57-b2d5-76c18fac1fcf)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/00e9661e-2b7e-414d-8c2c-f4d4f47b8b55)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/47c99681-6ca9-484b-ab33-102a4021cd92)

JPMorgan is even building its own solution. But 99% of the investors, companies, and advisors we talk to don't want to own this themselves, or don't have the resources to. That's where Pennant comes in, and it's why we're winning business out of the gate.\
\
**Why Pennant is better:** Pennant isn't a better proxy advisor. We're building something bigger: the AI-native operating system for corporate governance, built by former proxy voters and technologists, a team that cast these votes and shipped the software at institutional scale.

Pennant gives institutional investors, and the advisors and companies they engage with, voting and governance intelligence to act on their own principles at scale. Legacy tools follow rigid rules; Pennant reasons through each ballot item, inbound email, and engagement question the way your team would, handling the clear calls and flagging the nuanced ones, keeping people in the driver's seat.

As one of our customers put it last week, “\[incumbent xyz\] can handle our routine stuff for another year, but we’re thrilled to use Pennant for the custom heavy-lifting that we’ve been wanting to do for a long time, and use you for everything from there.”

Pennant also serves the other side of the vote: public companies, law firms, and bankers who need to read their shareholder base and predict risk before the annual meeting. Same data, bigger market. The market at the intersection of investing and corporate governance is estimated at well over $200 billion, and it remains largely unserved by today's tools.

**Traction:** Pennant is live with paying enterprise customers, including one of the largest US public pension plans, a Top AmLaw 100 firm, and leading governance advisors. We're partnered with a top global asset manager as a design partner and are actively engaged with S&P 500 companies. Before YC S26, Pennant was selected for Palantir's Startup Fellowship (Cohort 002).

**Why us:** We've known each other for 15 years, since our undergrad days at Cornell, and started our careers on the same analyst desk at BlackRock building tech products for these exact customers. We have a rare pairing: direct industry experience as the customer, plus the engineering chops to ship fast and earn trust.

After BlackRock, Ryan (CEO) was the customer for 6+ years, voting proxies at 3,000+ company meetings and advising Fortune 100 companies on how to win critical votes at PJT Partners. He used Glass Lewis and ISS every day.

Tommy (CTO) took the technical path, shipping products at BlackRock before earning his Harvard MBA and founding Mindware, where he built workflow-ready infrastructure for AI agents. He was building agentic AI before "agents" were hot, and Pennant is where his engineering background meets Ryan's proxy-voting expertise.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Compliance teams at institutional trading firms still spend hours manually sifting through mountains of data across recorded calls, chats, and trade records to investigate activity and produce defensible audit trails. Determining what matters requires not only finding the right data, but also interpreting activity against applicable regulations and the firm’s own policies and procedures. TovenAI is building a platform of AI agents that connects to their systems, assembles the evidence, and surfaces what matters for compliance teams at these firms—think the sales and trading businesses at banks like Bank of America and specialist brokerages like Marex.

We are live at one of the top 10 institutional trading firms in the U.S., with multiple AI agents delivering value through our platform.

<https://youtu.be/02IMKFk38IU>

## **What we built**

TovenAI’s agents analyze activity across existing communications and trading systems using each firm’s policies, procedures, and applicable regulations as context, assembling the relevant evidence for compliance teams.

Our trade-reconstruction agent rebuilds the full sequence of a trade, links every event to its source evidence, and reduces the process from around four hours to minutes. Our electronic-communications surveillance agent reduces the false-positive burden by 3× and, in a head-to-head evaluation, delivered roughly 7× more value per alert reviewed than the market-leading incumbent.

Our platform supports several other compliance workflows, giving teams broader coverage with less manual work.

With prebuilt integrations to more than 30 systems – including Bloomberg, Cloud9, CME and NICE Actimize – firms can evaluate TovenAI on their own data in under a week without replacing their existing stack.

## **Why us**

We met eight years ago at Stanford. Batu later worked as a quantitative research engineer at Citadel Global Quantitative Strategies, building AI systems for quantitative research. Sam was a machine learning engineer at Meta, working on its ads recommendation systems.

We work closely with our customers and sit besides compliance officers every day. This gives us a rapid feedback loop, lets us see their workflows firsthand, and allows us to redesign compliance operations with AI at their core.

Sam’s mother spent her 15-year career in risk and compliance and was our first sounding board as we began exploring the space.

## **Our ask**

We would love introductions to compliance leaders at firms with institutional trading businesses.

Think the sales and trading divisions of banks like **JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citizens**, as well as specialist brokerages like **TP ICAP and Marex**. We are interested in firms of all sizes, from specialist brokerages to the largest global banks.

If you know a broker or trader at one of these firms, they can likely connect us with someone on their compliance team.

launches.title: Florin: A full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters
launches.tagline: Autonomously places hard-to-price risks in seconds
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Florin is a full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters. Software takes a submission from a raw intake form to a bindable quote in seconds. Instead of matching a business to a class code, it verifies what the business actually does using satellite imagery, permits, public records and social media, then prices it by simulating tens of thousands of ways its next few years could go.

<https://youtu.be/BaXtkdP6_nc>

**What we do and why**

Insurance prices risk with class codes. An underwriter receives an application PDF, matches the business to a row in a rate table, and quotes off that row. This breaks in two ways. Applications are incomplete or wrong, so the price is built on bad inputs. And when a business does not fit any row, either because it is genuinely new (robotics, AI, autonomy) or because the table says the whole class or state is unprofitable, the answer is a declination. That is why carriers are exiting entire states and why a three-year-old industry can barely buy coverage at any price.

Florin replaces the table with evidence. It ingests the submission directly, no intake team. It builds its own picture of the business from the outside: aerial imagery of the actual premises, permits and public records, even the insured's social media, where it has caught operations that were never disclosed on the application. From that verified picture it runs simulations of the business's possible futures and produces a quote you can bind in seconds. No human touches the file.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109455&key=user_uploads/3776296/18477520-2b5a-4473-a727-92daf673768d)

**Team**

\- Shaurya Aggarwal built silicon on Google's next-generation TPU team

\- Amol Pant was on Tesla's supercomputer team, designed rovers for NASA, and was early at a Thiel backed robotics startup

\- Aydin Sorensen was early at Terrafirma, a construction robotics company that recently raised $115M

Shaurya and I have been best friends since middle school, and Aydin and I were roommates in college. We all lived together in Seattle for 2 years.
